question: Sultan Azlan Shah Cup is held in _________ .
solution:
The correct answer is __**Malaysia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• The Sultan Azlan Shah Cup is an annual international men’s field hockey tournament.

• It is held in Ipoh, Perak, Malaysia.

• The tournament is named after Sultan Azlan Shah, a former President of the Malaysian Hockey Federation and a keen hockey enthusiast.

• The tournament was first held in 1983 and has since become a prominent event in the international field hockey calendar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Field Hockey:**

• Field hockey is a team sport of the hockey family. The game can be played on grass, watered turf, artificial turf, or synthetic field, as well as an indoor boarded surface.

• Each team plays with ten field players and a goalkeeper.

• The object of the game is to score more goals than the opposition.

• Field hockey is widely played across the world and is the national sport of countries like India and Pakistan.

• **Ipoh:**

• Ipoh is the capital city of the Malaysian state of Perak.

• It is located by the Kinta River and is approximately 180 km north of Kuala Lumpur and 123 km southeast of George Town in neighbouring Penang.

• Ipoh is known for its limestone hills and caves, including the well-known cave temples of Perak Tong and Sam Poh Tong.

• The city is also a gateway to the Cameron Highlands, a popular hill station in Malaysia.

• **Sultan Azlan Shah:**

• Sultan Azlan Shah was the ninth Yang di-Pertuan Agong (King) of Malaysia and the 34th Sultan of Perak.

• He was an avid supporter of field hockey and contributed significantly to the development of the sport in Malaysia.

• In recognition of his contributions, the Sultan Azlan Shah Cup was established and named in his honor.

• He served as the President of the Malaysian Hockey Federation and was also an honorary life member of the International Hockey Federation (FIH).
